turns.assessment: All four degraded services share lightpath och87, while other lightpaths and the line-system monitors remain unchanged. Normal incoming OCM readings at S24 localize the loss after the incoming channel monitor, making a channel-specific attenuation drift in S24's drop WSS the best explanation; the modest loss can remain alarm-free and without a BER change. The later pump-current change on S03-S07 is off the affected path and is likely incidental.

proposals.rationale: A drop-WSS attenuation increase at S24 would reduce only och87 at trx.och87.a while upstream OCMs and other channels remain normal. Every degraded service depends on och87.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local defect could affect only och87 measurements at S24, but the absence of a pre-FEC BER change makes a receiver penalty less compelling than actual channel attenuation before the receiver.
A channel-specific launch attenuation at the far-end ROADM could affect och87 alone, but downstream OCMs should then have detected its power reduction.
